title: The Iron Clock
premise: In 1848, in the river city of Vellmark, Cyrus Okafor — a mapmaker's apprentice hiding her identity behind a dead brother's name — is finishing the great atlas her master died protecting when imperial orders arrive to seize the workshop and everyone in it. A sealed letter hidden in the atlas's final plate proves the Okafor family was named as conspirators by someone inside the guild, and Cyrus realizes the only way to save them is to carry the evidence herself through three checkpoints before the spring ice breaks and the river closes to smugglers. Betrayed by the one ally she trusted, she must choose between erasing herself forever or signing her true name to the map that will expose the plot. She delivers the atlas at dawn as the ice cracks, claiming her name and her place in the world at last.
about_author: Mara Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten maps and the marginalia of people history overlooked. She writes historical fiction about those who measured the world while remaining unmeasured themselves.

chapters.title: The Weight of Rivers
chapters.summary: Cyrus Okafor, working under her dead brother's name, inks the final coastline of Master Aldous Verren's atlas in their besieged workshop. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by grief — she measures everything in what can be carried, because leaving has always been the family trade.

chapters.title: Orders in the Morning Fog
chapters.summary: Imperial clerks post seizure notices: the workshop, its contents, and its household are forfeit within thirty days. Cyrus watches neighbors avert their eyes. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve; invisibility, her lifelong armor, begins to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: What the Master Died For
chapters.summary: Sorting Verren's papers, Cyrus finds his journal describing a sealed letter hidden in the atlas's final copper plate — proof of a plot naming the Okafor family. POV: Cyrus with flashback fragments of Verren. Emotional beat: the dead man's trust lands like an inheritance she never asked for.

chapters.title: The Guildhall's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Cyrus visits the Cartographers' Guild to petition an extension and glimpses Deputy Surveyor Halloway burning documents. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the plot reaches high, and the guild that should protect mapmakers is complicit.

chapters.title: A Name Not Her Own
chapters.summary: Cyrus's mother, Adaeze, reveals how they took brother Chidi's identity after his death at sea, and begs Cyrus to run south as they always have. POV: alternating Cyrus and Adaeze. Emotional beat: love expressed as flight versus Cyrus's first stubborn refusal to disappear.

chapters.title: The Copper Plate
chapters.summary: Working nights, Cyrus pries the backing from the final plate and finds the sealed letter: names, dates, payments routing through Halloway to a magistrate. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and purpose fused — the evidence is real, and now so is her target.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One River
chapters.summary: Cyrus maps her route: the Tollgate Bridge, the Customs House, the Ice Wharf — each requiring papers she cannot forge alone. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the mapmaker becomes the mapped; for once she plots a route with herself as the cargo.

chapters.title: An Ally with Ink-Stained Fingers
chapters.summary: Cyrus confides in Tomas Rehl, a journeyman printer who owes Verren his life, and he agrees to forge transit passes. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: cautious warmth — the first person in years to see Cyrus clearly, which is both comfort and exposure.

chapters.title: The Tollgate Bridge
chapters.summary: First checkpoint: Cyrus crosses disguised as a courier among fish carts, the letter sewn into her coat lining, while a guard reads her forged pass twice. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: white-knuckle triumph — she can do this, and doing it changes how she walks.

chapters.title: Halloway Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Deputy Surveyor Halloway searches the workshop 'for inventory,' lingering over the atlas's missing final plate. Adaeze lies smoothly; Cyrus nearly breaks. POV: alternating Cyrus and Adaeze. Emotional beat: the hunt has begun, and home no longer shields anyone.

chapters.title: Ice on the Window
chapters.summary: A rare hard freeze stalls the river; the ice-break deadline looms larger as patrols double. Cyrus hides the letter inside a hollowed surveyor's rule. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: claustrophobic patience — winter, her old enemy, now guards her secret.

chapters.title: The Customs House Clerk
chapters.summary: Second checkpoint: a weary clerk, Elias Brandt, recognizes Verren's hand on Cyrus's forged papers and hesitates — then stamps them, whispering that Verren once saved his daughter. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: unexpected grace; kindness survives inside the machine.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Green Ink
chapters.summary: Cyrus discovers one of her practice passes copied in green ink — Tomas has been reporting to Halloway since before she trusted him. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: devastation sharpening into fury; the wound of being truly seen, then sold.

chapters.title: Running the Rooftops
chapters.summary: Evading arrest after Tomas tips Halloway, Cyrus flees across Vellmark's rooftops with the surveyor's rule, sheltered briefly by dockworkers who owe the Okafors old debts. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the invisible girl discovers she belongs to more people than she knew.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Choice
chapters.summary: Halloway detains Adaeze, offering her freedom for the letter. Adaeze, who taught Cyrus to vanish, instead burns her own false papers and declares her daughter's true name aloud. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: the mother who preached flight chooses standing still — and standing for something.

chapters.title: The Ice Wharf
chapters.summary: Third checkpoint: Cyrus, half-frozen, bluffs past the wharfmaster using Elias Brandt's stamped manifest, the letter hidden in a crate of Verren's instruments. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: desperate competence — every skill her master taught her spent at once.

chapters.title: Tomas at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Tomas intercepts Cyrus at the embankment, torn between debt to Halloway and shame; Cyrus gives him the choice Halloway never gave her. He lets her pass, then turns himself in. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered without absolution — costly, human, unresolved.

chapters.title: The Night the River Held Its Breath
chapters.summary: Cyrus waits in a smuggler's cellar for the ice to break, writing her testimony and signing it with her full true name for the first time. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: stillness before rupture; identity claimed on paper before it is claimed aloud.

chapters.title: When the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: At dawn the river cracks open. Cyrus boards a grain barge carrying the letter toward the provincial assizes, pursued by Halloway along the quay. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror braided together — the world literally breaking open around her act of courage.

chapters.title: The Atlas Entered as Evidence
chapters.summary: Before the assizes, Cyrus presents the completed atlas itself — Verren's life's work with her own signed plates — alongside the letter. The court accepts both. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vindication that feels less like victory than arrival; her work speaks her name.

chapters.title: Halloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: The plot unravels: Halloway arrested, the magistrate implicated, the seizure orders rescinded. Adaeze is freed, and the workshop restored — but Verren's death is ruled an accident, a bitter compromise. POV: alternating Cyrus and Adaeze. Emotional beat: justice, partial and imperfect, still worth having.

chapters.title: Signed in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Spring: Cyrus completes the atlas's title page, signing 'Cyrus Okafor, Mapmaker' beneath her master's name, and hangs the first printed copy where the whole street can see. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted — she stays, visible at last, and begins mapping what comes next.
